profiles.summary: My campaign is focused on five key priorities.

priorities.title: Making Rhode Island More Affordable
priorities.summary: Working to lower the cost of living by addressing rising utility costs, expanding consumer protections, supporting affordable housing, and ensuring working families can keep more of what they earn.

priorities.title: Expanding Access to Healthcare
priorities.summary: Strengthening our healthcare workforce by improving provider retention, supporting primary care, increasing access to preventive and mental healthcare, and ensuring every Rhode Islander can access quality, affordable care.

priorities.title: Government Accountability and Transparency
priorities.summary: Promoting ethical, transparent government that is responsive to residents, protects taxpayer dollars, and restores public trust through greater accountability.

priorities.title: Building a Stronger Economy for Working Families
priorities.summary: Supporting small businesses, investing in workforce development, creating good-paying jobs, and ensuring economic growth benefits working families, not just large corporations.

priorities.title: Investing in Safe, Healthy, and Sustainable Communities
priorities.summary: Improving infrastructure, supporting public education, expanding clean energy that reduces costs for consumers, protecting our environment, and creating neighborhoods where families can thrive.

profiles.summary: Michael J. Riley, known as Lou, is a third-generation Scituate resident, solo-practice real estate attorney, husband, and father of four running in House District 41.

priorities.title: Repeal the Assault Weapons Ban
priorities.summary: The assault weapons ban took effect on July 1 and, in his view, will not stop crime while turning law-abiding residents into criminals. He says he will vote to repeal it.

priorities.title: Local Control of Zoning and Land Use
priorities.summary: If something is getting built in Scituate, he believes Scituate should decide. He says the state keeps overriding local planning and zoning boards and that he will fight to restore local control.

priorities.title: Taxes and Cost of Living
priorities.summary: He points to the conveyance-tax increase, Rhode Island's non-portable estate tax starting below $2 million, the non-owner-occupied surcharge, and business surtaxes as reasons it is getting more expensive both to live in Rhode Island and to pass assets on to family.

priorities.title: Schools and Parental Voice
priorities.summary: He wants more money to reach classrooms, more secure school buildings, and a stronger voice for parents. As a father of four, he says this is a personal priority.

priorities.title: Keeping Doctors in Rhode Island
priorities.summary: He argues that long waits for primary-care appointments, residents driving to Massachusetts, and doctors closing practices or leaving the state all show a healthcare access problem that the legislature should address.

profiles.summary: My campaign is focused on five key priorities.

priorities.title: Healthcare
priorities.summary: Medicaid is a lifeline for our most vulnerable neighbors. Cutting Medicaid reimbursements affects everyone by driving providers out of business and worsening shortages that limit access to care. Garman supports increasing Medicaid reimbursements, especially for substance use disorder treatment and other mental health care, and ultimately transitioning to Medicare for All.

priorities.title: Housing
priorities.summary: Garman describes housing as a human right and homelessness as a policy failure that requires urgent action. He supports prioritizing investment in affordable and low-income housing while also using tools such as enhanced historic rehabilitation tax credits to restore historic buildings and increase housing supply.

priorities.title: Energy and the Environment
priorities.summary: Garman says climate change is an existential threat and supports continued investment in clean energy. He also supports state-level incentives to offset the elimination of federal tax credits for residential solar panels and electric vehicles.

priorities.title: Immigration
priorities.summary: Garman says Rhode Island should protect immigrant communities and reject the demonization of immigrants. He supports extending Providence-style protections statewide by blocking local and state law enforcement from collaborating with ICE unless required by federal law or a judicial warrant.

priorities.title: Tax Equity
priorities.summary: Garman argues that Rhode Island's tax structure should be more equitable and that those with the most should pay their fair share to support safety-net programs such as Medicaid and SNAP. He supports investing in public services and safety-net programs so Rhode Island is affordable and attractive for residents.

profiles.summary: Campaign priorities summarized from Jonathon Acosta's published campaign website.

priorities.title: Criminal Justice Reform
priorities.summary: Supports reforming solitary confinement and restrictive housing, including oversight of its use in Rhode Island correctional facilities.

priorities.title: Health Care
priorities.summary: Supports protecting and expanding health-care access, including Medicaid, and opposing reductions that would restrict coverage or services.

priorities.title: Progressive Taxation
priorities.summary: Supports a higher income-tax rate on high-income earners. The 2026 proposal would add a 3% rate on taxable income above $640,000; earlier versions used a lower inflation-adjusted threshold.

priorities.title: Housing
priorities.summary: Supports expanding affordable housing and policies intended to increase the development and preservation of affordable homes.

priorities.title: Jobs and Wages
priorities.summary: Supports policies aimed at increasing wages and improving economic conditions for working families.

priorities.title: Climate and Clean Energy
priorities.summary: Supports policies to accelerate clean-energy development and address climate change.

priorities.title: Education
priorities.summary: Supports increased public-education funding and additional support for high-need students, multilingual learners, and other special populations.

priorities.summary: Continue work related to a study commission on safe staffing in hospitals, with an emphasis on worker and patient safety.
